prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: 公式文本 · 物理量 (language zh-CN).
Grid: 5 columns × 5 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "物理量" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 123px
  col 2: header "符号" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 31px
  col 3: header "公式" · longest unbreakable word 65px · one-line width 91px
  col 4: header "单位" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 31px
  col 5: header "说明" · longest unbreakable word 77px · one-line width 274px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 360px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"A compact physics formula reference: for each quantity it gives the symbol, defining formula, unit and a short explanatory note, for lookup and quick comparison rather than continuous reading.","reading":"Readers scan row by row: quantity name → symbol → formula → unit, then drop into the note. Columns 2–4 form a compact technical core, while 说明 is secondary but contains constants and caveats that must remain legible.","groups":["Columns 2 符号, 3 公式 and 4 单位 belong together: they are the technical identity of each quantity and should stay adjacent and compact.","Column 1 物理量 is the row entry point and label.","Column 5 说明 is explanatory annotation and can absorb wrapping."],"keep_intact":["symbols such as E_k, F, E","formula tokens and operators; ideally whole formulas, at minimum unbreakable terms such as ½mv² and G·m₁m₂/r²","units J and N","scientific notation such as 6.674×10⁻¹¹","short headers 符号, 公式, 单位"],"may_wrap":["物理量 names such as 理想气体状态方程","说明 prose and notes","formulas at = or spaces if necessary, but not inside tokens"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[54,51,105,51,98],"idea":"Formula-first: give 公式 nearly its full one-line width and protect 说明 tokens, while 物理量 wraps to two characters per line."},{"name":"B","widths":[73,51,86,51,98],"idea":"Balanced row scan: keep every unbreakable token and the 物理量 header intact, let formulas wrap at operators, and give 说明 a stable readable width."},{"name":"C","widths":[66,40,86,40,127],"idea":"Description-led: compress 符号 and 单位 to token-width tag columns with stacked headers, freeing width for the explanatory 说明 column."}]}
